title: What God Looks for in a Wife
paragraphs:
What God Looks for in a Wife
The Forgotten Beauty Heaven Still Notices When the World Looks Away
There is a question hidden deep inside the hearts of many women that rarely gets spoken out loud.
It surfaces after another failed relationship.
After scrolling through photos that seem to suggest everyone else is more beautiful, more desired, more loved, more chosen.
It lingers in the silence after prayers that seem unanswered.
"What does God actually look for in a wife?"
What does the Creator of heaven and earth Himself consider beautiful?
Because God's standard has never been based on the things people spend billions of dollars trying to achieve.
And perhaps nowhere is this truth more beautifully revealed than in one of the most misunderstood passages in Scripture.
When the prophet Samuel was sent to anoint Israel's future king, he naturally assumed God would choose the tallest, strongest, most impressive man in the room.
"Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart." (1 Samuel 16:7)
And if this is how God chooses kings, should we expect Him to choose wives differently?
The Bible never presents godly womanhood as perfection.
In fact, some of Scripture's most remarkable women carried stories that looked more like scandals than success stories.
The woman at the well had multiple broken relationships.
Mary Magdalene was delivered from demonic oppression.
Yet God rewrote every one of their stories.
Because Heaven specializes in transforming what people write off.
That is the heartbeat of the Gospel.
One of the clearest descriptions of a godly wife appears in Proverbs 31.
Ironically, many women read it and feel discouraged.
A woman who seems capable of doing everything perfectly.
But that was never the point.
The chapter is not celebrating perfection.
The Hebrew phrase often translated "virtuous woman" is:
But the word chayil means strength, courage, valor, moral excellence, and noble character.
This is not a weak woman.
This is not a passive woman.
This is a woman whose life is anchored in God.
A woman who remains faithful when compromise would be easier.
A woman who chooses obedience when nobody is watching.
A woman whose identity comes from God rather than public approval.
The world teaches women to ask:
And character is forged where nobody can see.
In choosing integrity when deception would be easier.
In remaining faithful when nobody would know otherwise.
One of the most beautiful verses in Scripture regarding biblical womanhood appears in 1 Peter 3:4.
Peter continues by describing a gentle and quiet spirit as being of great worth before God.
Society changes its standards every decade.
The beauty God treasures most cannot be purchased.
It is cultivated through walking with Christ.
Perhaps that is why Jesus Himself never seemed impressed by what impressed everyone else.
Others saw a widow giving two small coins.
Jesus saw a heart fully surrendered.
Others saw a sinful woman weeping.
Because Jesus sees what others miss.
Maybe someone reading this has spent years believing your mistakes disqualified you.
Maybe you carry shame from decisions you wish you could undo.
Maybe your testimony contains chapters you hope nobody ever discovers.
Maybe your past still whispers accusations.
The Gospel does not begin with worthy people earning God's love.
The Gospel begins with sinners receiving God's grace.
"But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."
Not after we cleaned ourselves up.
Not after we fixed every flaw.
The Greek word used for grace throughout the New Testament is:
Because if salvation itself is based on grace, then biblical womanhood is not about earning God's approval.
It is about responding to God's love.
A wife after God's heart is not a woman who never fails.
She is a woman who keeps returning to Jesus.
When she falls, she runs to Christ.
When she struggles, she runs to Christ.
When she feels weak, she runs to Christ.
When she feels unworthy, she runs to Christ.
Because her confidence is not in herself.
Her confidence is in her Savior.
That is the kind of beauty Heaven celebrates.
The kind that survives seasons when external beauty inevitably fades.
"Charm is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised."
A life oriented around pleasing God above everything else.
That is what God looks for in a wife.
A woman who chooses Christ above the applause of the world.
And perhaps the most beautiful part of all is this:
God is not merely looking for godly wives.
Scripture repeatedly reveals that God Himself is preparing a Bride.
Ephesians describes Jesus loving His Bride and giving Himself for her.
The story of marriage ultimately points beyond human relationships to the Gospel itself.
A love stronger than death itself.
That means the ultimate answer to what God looks for in a wife is found in what Christ is creating in all who belong to Him.
A life surrendered to His Lordship.
A soul that treasures Him above everything else.
And if your story currently feels broken, unfinished, messy, or stained by regret, remember this:
And your story can be rewritten too.
Because the cross was never about preserving perfect people.
The cross was about redeeming broken people.
This may have touched a place you've kept hidden for a long time.
And if this message reminded you of God's grace, share it boldly. Every share becomes another opportunity for someone to encounter the hope of Christ.
The world keeps asking women to become someone else.
Jesus keeps inviting them to come home.
